A.explanation: This inverts the $x$ length fraction and does not match the balance $V_1$ across length $x$ and $V_2$ across length $L-x$.

B.explanation: This compares $x$ to the whole length $L$, but $V_2$ is balanced only against the $JY$ section of length $L-x$.

C.explanation: This is the inverse ratio $V_2/V_1$, since $V_1$ belongs to the $x$ section and $V_2$ belongs to the $L-x$ section.

D.explanation: At balance $V_1$ equals the p.d. across $x$ and $V_2$ equals the p.d. across $L-x$, so $V_1/V_2 = x/(L-x)$ for the uniform wire.

hints: Notice the wording lamp is off, so there is no current in branch $S$ and the junction of $R_1$ and $R_2$ must be at the same potential as the contact $J$.
Connect $V_1$ to the wire section $XJ$ of length $x$ and $V_2$ to the wire section $JY$ of length $L-x$, because $R_1$ joins $X$ and $R_2$ joins $Y$.
Use that XY is uniform, so p.d. along the wire is proportional to length, then form the ratio of the $x$ p.d. to the $L-x$ p.d.
walkthrough: Lamp off means zero current through $S$, so no p.d. is lost in $S$ and the $R_1$-$R_2$ junction is at the same potential as point $J$ on the wire.
Therefore $V_1$, between $X$ and the junction, equals the p.d. between $X$ and $J$. That section has length $x$.
Similarly $V_2$, between the junction and $Y$, equals the p.d. between $J$ and $Y$. That section has length $L-x$.
For uniform wire of length $L$, resistance and p.d. are proportional to length, so $V_1 \propto x$ and $V_2 \propto L-x$.
Dividing gives $V_1/V_2 = x/(L-x)$. This is option D.
